amanda_support: FYI ops, several customers reporting intermittent 502/504s hitting the hosted embeddings/chat endpoints over the last 40m. Mostly during large streaming/batch requests. attaching one trace id: trace=trc_0a1b2c3d

jordan_sre: thx. any repro steps from the customer? approximate QPS?

amanda_support: Customer sent repro: batching 256 embeddings in one request with streaming=true, sustained ~200rps per client for ~30s. saw 502s spike and then degraded success rate. customer says errors started after ~09:12 UTC.

sophie_runtime: grabbing envoy and edge logs now. Can you confirm tenant and sample request id?

amanda_support: tenant=acme-corp, request_id=req_9f8e7d6c, trace=trc_0a1b2c3d

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline: auth-cache v3.1.2 -> rolled 2026-03-16T08:50:00Z to prod small canary

jordan_sre: interesting — we had an auth-cache canary earlier. checking if canary overlap correlates. sophie paste envoy logs?

sophie_runtime: paste logs (redacted):
```
[2026-03-16T09:12:34.123Z] envoy info: upstream reset before response: connection failure, reset reason: remote_reset
[2026-03-16T09:12:34.124Z] envoy warn: stream reset by peer: RST_STREAM code=2
[2026-03-16T09:12:34.125Z] edge-auth-plugin: cache miss, backend_validate latency=120ms
[2026-03-16T09:12:34.126Z] edge-auth-plugin: cache_eviction: mem_growth=+8MB, entries=124000
[2026-03-16T09:12:34.127Z] envoy error: upstream connection closed before response completed
```

luis_prodeng: that mem_growth line stands out — looks like auth cache entries spiking. if auth plugin blocks or GC happens it could hold worker threads and cause pooling exhaustion on h2 connections.

jordan_sre: correlate with metrics: h2 conn_count, active_streams, worker_cpu. sophiE attach metric snippets?

sophie_runtime: metrics snapshot around spike: h2_active_streams=1900 -> drop to 200 as proxies return 502s; h2_conn_open=14000; envoy_worker_cpu spiking 95% for envoy-worker-3; auth-backend 5xx_rate increased from 0.1% -> 12% in same window.

amanda_support: customer also shared curl that repros locally for them: they used very large POST with multiple embed inputs; here's an anonymized repro they provided:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\ 
  -d '{"inputs":["long text...", "..." /* ~256 items */], "stream":true}' \\ 
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings"
```

jordan_sre: quick hypothesis: auth-cache mem growth + auth backend transient 5xx causes edge auth plugin to synchronously validate many requests, blocking envoy worker threads -> h2 connection pool stalls -> upstream resets and 502/504. also streaming large bodies exacerbates connection windowing.

luis_prodeng: agree. two immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily reduce max batch size at ingress (throttle >128) 2) increase auth-cache TTL/fill-rate to avoid backend calls. also rotate traffic off envoy-worker-3.

sophie_runtime: doing a config patch to reduce ingress max_batch_size to 128 for hosted-api (hotfix). rolling to 5% -> 25% canary now.

ops-bot: Rollout event: ingress-config v2026-03-16-1155 -> canary 5%

amanda_support: relaying to customer: asking them to try <=128 batch or sequential smaller calls in the meantime.

jordan_sre: longer term fix: auth-cache v3.1.3 with bounded memory and background eviction + nonblocking validation path. we should revert canary v3.1.2 if correlation holds. requesting urgent patch from runtime team.

sophie_runtime: start building v3.1.3 patch now. adding a fallback that returns 429 instead of synchronously hitting backend when cache is saturated.

luis_prodeng: also add metrics alert for auth_cache_entries and envoy_worker_cpu >80% sustained.

amanda_support: customer confirmed reduced errors after we asked them to lower batch size; still seeing occasional 502s but much lower. they appreciate the workaround. :relieved:

jordan_sre: plan for next 2 hours: 1) continue canary ingress throttle (5->25->100), 2) halt v3.1.2 auth-cache rollout if any host shows mem_growth, 3) ship v3.1.3 with bounded cache + async fallback within 6h. anyone object?

sophie_runtime: ack. I'll also add a temporary proxy-level backpressure: limit concurrent streaming requests per-connection to 8.

ops-bot: Incident note added: INCIDENT-2026-0316-EDGE-502S-AUTHCACHE. severity: P2.

amanda_support: tagging customer update: "We've applied temporary ingress limits and recommended smaller batches — our engineering team is deploying a targeted fix to the auth cache. We'll update in ~4h."

jordan_sre: closing thread for now, will re-open if rollback/patch needed. leaving traces and artifacts in #incidents. thx everyone. :thumbsup:
